body:
The supported MIM release preserves unsupported scientific claims for further curation. SSSOM finalization in #731 completes the disposition review for all **3,018 mapping rows**: **1,763 supported** and **1,255 withheld**. The complete source graph remains semantically unapproved.

Current mapping snapshot: [mim-sssom-2026-09-21](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/releases/tag/mim-sssom-2026-09-21). Its separate `withheld_mappings.sssom.tsv` preserves every withheld source row; `mapping-dispositions.tsv` records all 3,018 decisions, reasons and evidence references. Missing support does not necessarily establish that a claim is false. Non-exact mapping relations, weak exact-match evidence, unresolved aliases and identity conflicts remain withheld.

The trait-synonym source cleanup in #703 is now complete: 46 activity phrases across 39 records are retained as rejected provenance. The original negative #724 decision remains archived; the corrected Aromatic Compound row has a separate evidence-bound review. Adversarial review #730 fixes publication and integrity defects by source correction, precise withholding and regression checks. Closing #730 does not declare the withheld source claims scientifically corrected.

The [earlier KGX snapshot](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/releases/tag/mim-supported-2026-09-21) remains historical: 4,587 nodes, 2,112 edges, 1,603 mappings and 2,411 excluded assertions. The new SSSOM supersedes that snapshot's mapping selection; a corresponding new KGX publication is still pending. Current graph review ledgers account for 2,251 excluded assertions and preserve 1,735 open major/blocking historical findings. These counts overlap and are not additive.

Priority evidence gaps in the current source corpus:

- The 1,255 withheld mapping rows in the new lossless SSSOM backlog.
- 662 prediction-only roles and 11 roles without evidence.
- 24 additional unverified role promotions: generic mineral labels had become trace-element, iron, phosphate, or sulfur requirements, and a generic growth-factor label had become a vitamin claim. Review #720 records the affected assertions.
- 43 component assertions requiring the original source preparation, including the unresolved PYGS abbreviation and TYGVS formulation differences.
- The flattened CMC/PY/horse-serum expression remains AMBIGUOUS after withdrawal of its false single-mixture identity.
- Other record-level findings remain explicit in the full disposition ledger.

Resolve each claim from its exact source identity, organism and preparation; add content-bound scientific dispositions and regenerate the affected artifacts. Do not bulk approve from chemical ancestry, name patterns, citation presence or structural validation. New evidence may move claims into the supported release only after review.

See [standalone SSSOM reproduction instructions](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/main/docs/SSSOM_RELEASE.md) and [mapping review evidence](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/tree/main/reports/sssom_completion_20260921). This issue remains open for scientific curation after #731.
title: Curate the claims excluded from the reviewed MIM release

body:
The remaining half of #409. That issue closed on the **predicate** disagreement — 249 flips, now 0, after fixes on both sides. The **row-count** difference is untouched and still blocks promotion.

Rebuilt from both merged mains:

```
published rows      2,944
rebuilt rows        2,891
published-only        155
rebuilt-only          102
predicate flips         0   <- fixed
```

`publish_sssom.py` refuses to promote when the row count would drop, and 2,891 < 2,944, so `just publish-sssom` remains unusable. That guard is doing its job — the point is that the underlying difference has not been reconciled.

## What the 155 are

All belong to records with a **MAPPED** status (90 exactMatch, 60 closeMatch, 5 narrowMatch). Two shapes:

- `MIM:X → kgmicrobe.compound:<slug>` / `kgmicrobe.ingredient:<slug>` where the record's own identifier is a `cas:` CURIE. The published file carries a registry row under the *minted* namespace; the builder's dual-emission block only emits a row for the identifier the record actually holds, so it writes the `cas:` row instead.
- Parent-anchor rows such as `PIPES buffer → CHEBI:39033`, where the record's identifier is `kgmicrobe.ingredient:pipes_buffer`.

The 102 rebuilt-only rows are the mirror image — registry rows the builder synthesises (including its Rule B1 backfill) that the published file either lacks or spells under a different namespace.

So this is not a semantic disagreement about any mapping. Both sides agree what maps to what; they disagree about **which registry CURIEs get their own row, and under which namespace**.

## Worth deciding

1. Whether a record whose identifier is `cas:` should ALSO carry a `kgmicrobe.compound:` registry row. Rule B1 requires one for asymmetric subjects; the published file appears to have them more broadly.
2. Whether `publish_sssom.py`'s guard should compare row counts at all, or compare row *sets* keyed on `(subject_id, object_id)` — a count is blind to 155 out and 102 in, which is the shape here.

Until (1) is settled the two artifacts cannot converge, and until then promotion stays blocked.
title: publish-sssom is still blocked: the builder emits 155 fewer registry rows than the published file

body:
Found in adversarial review of #528 (pre-existing; that PR neither caused nor worsened it).

17 records carry the same synonym text twice, compared casefolded:

```
Distilled_Water.yaml            'sterile dh2o'
Alk_So42.yaml                   'aluminum potassium sulfate'
Na2glycerophosphate5h2o.yaml    'na2glycerophosphate•5h2o(cas: 13408-09-8)'
Casein_Peptone.yaml             'casein hydrolysate', 'casein enzymic hydrolysate'
```

Count is identical on `origin/main`, so this predates the surface-form work. The
backfill's own duplicate check kept it from growing.

Low severity, but not nothing:

* `export_lists.py` emits one `label_index.csv` row per synonym, so a duplicate
  synonym produces two identical index rows for the same record. The lookup still
  resolves, but the index is larger than the corpus it describes and row counts stop
  being a usable measure of coverage — which is the number this work has been tracking
  throughout.
* The builder pipes synonyms into SSSOM `other`, where `_pipe` caps at
  `MAX_OTHER_ENTRIES = 50`. On a crowded row a duplicate consumes a slot that a distinct
  surface form would otherwise get, and the cap is documented as biting hardest on the
  hydrate families.

The fix is a de-duplicating pass over `synonyms`, casefolded, keeping the first
occurrence and preferring the more specific `synonym_type` when the duplicates disagree
(e.g. a `RAW_TEXT` and an `EXACT_SYNONYM` of the same string). Worth pairing with a guard
so it cannot recur, since several writers append synonyms and only some check first.
title: 17 records carry the same synonym twice, inflating the label index and the other cap

body:
Found in the adversarial review of #485. Low severity; a visibility gap, not a wrong value.

Of the 800 records that PR refreshes, **24 moved down**:

| record | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `DL-2-Methylbutyric acid` | 77 | 23 |
| `PIPES sesquisodium salt` | 67 | 36 |
| `L-Glutamic acid monopotassium salt monohydrate` | 44 | 16 |
| `NaNO` | 24 | 8 |
| `Bacitracin` | 10 | 1 |

An upward move is self-explaining — the old value was truncated or zero. A **downward** move is not: it says the record was previously credited with media it no longer matches. The likely cause is benign (CultureMech a28f4b041e changed identity resolution to go through a pinned MIM index, just before #337), but "the ingredient genuinely appears in fewer recipes" and "resolution stopped matching some recipes" are different facts and the report renders them identically.

`reports/occurrence_statistics_refresh.tsv` marks every change `REFRESHED` or `REFRESHED_SHARED_IDENTIFIER`. A `REFRESHED_DECREASED` marker — or just a direction column — would let a curator scan the 24 without recomputing from the old/new columns.

Worth pairing with #486: knowing *which* CultureMech vintage produced a decrease is what makes it interpretable.

Not blocking #485 — the values are correct as derived, and 24 rows out of 800 are inspectable by hand from the existing columns.
title: 24 refreshed counts moved DOWN and the report does not distinguish them

body:
Found in the adversarial review of #485.

That PR replaces 800 records' counts because the old values' provenance was lost: nobody could tell that a `media_count` of 50 came from `data['media_occurrences'][:50]` rather than from reality, and the only way I established it was a distribution spike.

**The replacements have the same gap.** The curation event records the before/after numbers and cites the issue:

> occurrence_statistics 50/1579 -> 1839/1839 (media_count/total_occurrences), derived from distinct CultureMech recipe ids in the #337 occurrence table…

but not **which** occurrence table. There is no CultureMech commit sha, no scan date, no row count, no path. And `reports/` is gitignored, so `occurrence_statistics_refresh.tsv` — which holds the full 800-row correction table — is not committed either.

So the repo contains 800 fresh numbers and no record of the data they came from. Re-running six months from now against a different CultureMech vintage produces different numbers with no way to tell which run any given record reflects.

## Why this matters more than usual here

CultureMech is actively changing: #337 landed 19 hours before this refresh, and a28f4b041e ("Resolve ingredient identities through pinned MIM index") changed identity resolution just before it. **24 of the 800 counts moved *down*** — `DL-2-Methylbutyric acid` 77 → 23, `PIPES sesquisodium salt` 67 → 36 — which is plausible as re-resolution but indistinguishable from a partial scan without knowing the source.

## Fix

Record the source in the curation event and the report header:

- the CultureMech commit sha the table was generated from (or the table's own mtime/hash if the sha is unavailable);
- the table's total row count and distinct-recipe count, so a truncated or partial input is visible after the fact;
- the scan date.

Cheap, and it is exactly the property whose absence made the original defect take a distribution analysis to find.

Consider also committing the correction report rather than leaving it under gitignored `reports/`, or writing a small provenance stanza somewhere tracked.
title: The refreshed counts record no provenance — the same gap that made the old ones untraceable

body:
A CHEBI-grounding pass over MIM's ungrounded ingredients (CAS→CHEBI via the local ChEBI dbxref index, complex-ingredient resolver, non-chemical flagging), relying on MIM's curated data + kg-microbe. **Finding: MIM is already well-curated** — of ~2,206 ungrounded unified rows, the substantive results were a handful of corrections, not a mass grounding.

## Landed (reviewed clean by Fable 5)
- **PR #112** — CHEBI grounding + curation:
  - Gepotidacin `cas:1075236-89-3` → `CHEBI:747127` (skos:exactMatch; unique CAS dbxref + label-exact).
  - Glycogen from bovine liver: `cas:` FALLBACK → `CHEBI:28087` (glycogen), exactMatch (source qualifier).
  - Beef extract: removed erroneous `cas_rn 103-47-9` (that CAS is CHES / `CHEBI:44302` — a PubChem name-lookup false positive); stays on `FOODON:03302088`.
  - SSSOM reconciled in-sync; invariants A/B1/B2/B3 pass.
- **PR #113** — periodic `UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` refresh (3,853→3,937 rows, CHEBI 1,647→1,668). Reviewer confirmed 100% CHEBI internal consistency.

## Already-correct (curation queue items that needed no change)
- sn-glycerol-3-phosphate lithium salt → `CHEBI:15978` (NARROW_MATCH, matches sibling salts).
- carnitine-DL-HCl → `CHEBI:17126` (carnitine, stereo-unspecified parent — correct for a DL racemate).

## Open follow-ups
- [ ] **Audit PubChem-sourced `cas_rn` for other false-positives.** Beef extract's `103-47-9` (=CHES) was a name-lookup mis-assignment by `fetch_cas_rn_from_pubchem`. Cross-check `chemical_properties.cas_rn` (esp. on `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE`/complex records) against CHEBI/expected formula to catch other bad CAS.
- [ ] **45 flagged non-chemicals** need disposition (not CHEBI-groundable): ~10 placeholders ("See source for composition"), ~20 complex mixtures/solutions, ~7 environmental/media, ~8 buffers (borderline). Decide: leave UNMAPPED, map to FOODON/ENVO, or mark NON_CHEMICAL.
- [ ] **Complex-resolver NO_HIT peptones** (Peptone, Proteose peptone, Trypticase peptone, …) would map cleanly to **MICRO** (`MICRO:0000178` = peptone) — deferred; needs the `MICRO:` prefix added to the SSSOM curie_map + builder.
- [ ] **Possible pre-existing mis-mapping:** `Carnitine Hydrochloride` → `CHEBI:48601` "carnitinamide chloride" — carnitinamide is the amide (a different compound); a curator should confirm vs carnitine/carnitinium chloride.

Full pipeline report (per-tier counts, all candidates) is captured in PR #112's description. Spec + report live in the session scratchpad (`GROUNDING_SPEC.md`, `chebi_grounding_report.md`).
title: CHEBI grounding pass — results, curation report & open follow-ups
